summary: Multi-hop egress observed when pinning to EU — increased P99 latency; clarification on residency policy and routing heuristics
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a consistent P99 latency increase (~350-450ms) for requests pinned to eu-west when their traffic appears to traverse a US egress/edge before returning to EU serving instances. They are using Dedicated capacity with a strict region pin (project-level pin to eu-west). Customer wants: (1) explanation of why traffic might take a multi-hop path across regions despite pinning, (2) confirmation about whether any data leaves the EU region (egress for processing vs egress for routing), and (3) guidance or configuration to ensure single-region egress for residency guarantees.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference latency increase on P99 for EU users (from typical 140ms -> 500-600ms for some requests).
- User experience degradation for real-time inference endpoints used in production for trading insights.
- No reported data leak; main concern is latency and confirming residency guarantees for compliance.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (dedicated-23), capacity reserved in eu-west.
- API endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
- Customer region pin: project config pin_region = "eu-west" (strict).
- Time window observed: 2026-03-12 09:00 -> 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC
- Example request-id headers: x-request-id: fc9a1b2d-e7a5-4f2f-9a6e-1f2b3c4d5e6f

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Pin a project to eu-west in the Dedicated console.
2) Send 1000 small-generation requests (~40 tokens) from a client in eu-west.
3) Observe P50/P95/P99 on customer side and compare to Redwood Console per-token latency.
4) Filter requests where x-request-id matches observed high-p99 (example IDs included below).

Observed behavior:
- For ~3-5% of requests, traces show an outbound hop to an edge in us-east before the request reaches eu-west serving instance. This corresponds to a spike in P99.
- Redwood Console shows model served from eu-west instance, but traces include an extra network leg (edge -> core -> back to eu).
- No 5xx errors, request succeeds.

Expected behavior:
- All traffic for a project pinned to eu-west should be routed and processed within eu-west without cross-region egress for inference path. 

Logs and traces (redacted):
- Example trace snippet (customer-provided):
  - request-id: fc9a1b2d-e7a5-4f2f-9a6e-1f2b3c4d5e6f
  - client -> edge-eu-west-01 (20ms) -> api-gateway-us-east-03 (210ms) -> serving-eu-03 (45ms) -> response path 230ms -> total 505ms
- Console route logs (sample): "route decision: sticky-affinity-expired -> fallback-edge: us-east-03 -> selected: eu-west-serving-03"

Additional notes from customer:
- They recently toggled stickiness TTL from 24h to 15m as an attempt to improve load distribution across dedicated pool.
- They are concerned whether any sensitive data is leaving eu region (privacy/compliance).
comments: 2026-03-13 11:02 - Support (Asha Mehta): Thanks for the detailed repro and trace. We're triaging with infra. Can you confirm whether the requests with multi-hop show any different model-version or host tags?

2026-03-13 13:45 - Customer (S. Petrov, FinCloud): Confirmed model_version: gptx-3.8-16k@v12 for all traces. Host tags for all 'served' segments are eu-west. The odd leg is always an api-gateway located in us-east.
2026-03-13 16:20 - Support (Asha Mehta): Noted. Looping in Diego (networking) and runtime to check routing heuristics and sticky-affinity TTL handling.

2026-03-14 09:05 - Infra (Diego Alvarez): Initial finding: smart-routing fallback policy can select an edge in any region when sticky-affinity TTL is expired/violated and the local edge doesn't have a fresh cached route to the serving pod. The selected edge is used to orchestrate the request and may add a cross-region hop before the serving runtime is reached. Investigating whether this path causes egress of request payload beyond EU for processing, or only for control-plane routing.

2026-03-14 11:08 - Security (Mira O'Connor): From a compliance perspective, control-plane routing metadata does not contain customer prompt content. We need to confirm whether any KV cache or prefix tokens are being forwarded during control ops.
investigation_notes:
Preliminary hypothesis: Changing stickiness TTL to 15m exposed cases where the edge node that initially handled a client (and had a warm cached prefix/KV route) expired and another client connection hit a different edge that lacked the route. The smart-routing fallback currently may select the closest available control edge, which can be cross-region. That edge then coordinates with the eu-west serving pod resulting in a visible extra leg in traces. Need to validate whether this control-edge performs any token-level proxying vs only routing control/handshake.

What we've checked so far:
- Console logs show serving kept in eu-west and model served there (no model shard in us-east).
- No 5xx or auth failures.
- Network team captured packet counts and did not find full request bodies in control-plane traffic samples (redacted).

Open questions for engineering:
- Is the routing decision for fallback-edge strictly control-plane (no customer payload), or can it forward partial request payloads (e.g., prefix cache warmup)?
- Can we add a per-project enforcement flag to avoid selecting non-EU control edges when project pin is strict?
next_steps: 1) Networking to run a packet-level capture (redacted) for a set of 50 reproduced requests to confirm payload vs metadata content. 2) Runtime team to audit smart-routing codepath for fallback selection and document whether any customer tokens are proxied across the control edge. 3) If confirmed control-plane-only, update customer with mitigation (increase stickiness TTL or enable local-edge-residency-preference). 4) If payload crosses regions, propose quick mitigation: prefer 'strict-egress' option for dedicated projects or add explicit egress-region affinity flag. 5) Create follow-up INT ticket to consider adding enforcement in routing logic and update runbook.
requested_customer_action: Please produce 10 request-ids (x-request-id) that show the multi-hop behavior and confirm whether you have any IP allowlists or client-side proxy settings that might cause requests to originate from non-EU egress. Also, revert stickiness TTL to 24h for a 2-hour test window if feasible so we can validate whether the incidence rate drops.
workaround: Temporary: Recommend restoring stickiness TTL to previous 24h or enabling the 'prefer-local-edge' project flag (if you have it) to reduce cross-region fallback decisions. This should reduce the multi-hop occurrences while we validate routing behavior.
slo_notes: Customer is on Dedicated; provide timeline for root cause: initial acknowledgement within 4 hours was met. Targeting a technical update in 48 hours after packet capture and routing audit.
follow_up_tasks: INT-90011 audit smart-routing fallback to honor strict-pin egress preference
INT-90012 add observability metric: cross-region-fallback-count per project
